The anytime valid ledger operates as a sequential hypothesis test that dynamically evaluates incoming returns using exponential weights. It maintains a running e-value which grows with favorable outcomes and shrinks with adverse ones. The rejection boundary is defined by 1/α, where α is the significance level. When the e-value crosses this boundary, the null hypothesis is rejected. This mechanism ensures that even under adversarial conditions, the false positive rate remains controlled. The adversarial Monte-Carlo verification simulates numerous adversarial sequences to confirm that the ledger's performance does not degrade beyond acceptable margins. The freeze slate commitment primitive ensures data integrity by hashing all valid receipts into a deterministic commitment, preventing tampering or retroactive changes. These primitives form a coherent system where probabilistic guarantees are maintained through both internal validation and external consistency checks.
